subject: corn
author: ags/claude-opus-5-5
question: how tight is corn, and what does the WASDE usually do?

balance_view.text: US corn 2026/27 stocks-to-use is 11.3% [s8], the 42 percentile since 2007/08 [s9]: middle of the range, not tight. The October WASDE raised ending stocks by 282 million bushels [s10], within USDA's own average miss of 331 at this point of the season [s12]. Stocks at the start of September were 43.8% above their 5-year average [s19]. Abroad, Conab puts Brazil's 26/27 corn at 148.02 Mt [s20], and US export commitments are 9.1% below the same week of the prior three market years [s23].

curve_shape.text: No grain futures curve is stored, so carry is not measured.

positioning.text: Managed money in corn is at the 78.8462 percentile of three years [s5], cut 4.3973 pp on the week [s6]. Context, not a signal.

narrative_stage.text: No crop narrative in the news check is above its usual coverage.

what_changed: First corn card: no earlier card to compare.
would_change_view: A WASDE ending-stocks cut larger than USDA's usual miss.
Export commitments catching up with the same week of earlier years.
Conab cutting Brazil's second-crop corn in its next surveys.
inference: Read: on WASDE days (months without Grain Stocks) corn has been more volatile than the surrounding fortnight either side: 1.314 times [s29], paired t 5.2 [s30]. That is volatility, not direction. The direction proxy (the same-day move vs the stocks revision) is -1.1193% per sd [s31] (t -3.93 [s32]), but it rests on reports since 2021 and no consensus, so it is a weak, attenuated measure.
Read: ONI at 2.16 [s25], El Niño-side for 4 consecutive seasons [s26]; the literature links El Niño to small changes in maize yields (drivers.md, Iizumi et al. 2014), so no direction is read from it.
open_questions: A WASDE consensus (public survey averages) would turn the volatility playbook into a surprise playbook.
